name: Humanist Minimal
summary: Very few marks, each one made by a human hand. Warm, plain and calm: one idea, lots of space, imperfect lines on flat paper.

principles.title: The human hand
principles.rule: Every mark looks made by a person: ink lines with a slight wobble, shapes cut with scissors. Nothing looks generated, glossy or machine-perfect.

principles.title: Few marks
principles.rule: Minimal means fewer things, not thinner things. If a line, shape or word can go, it goes.

principles.title: One idea
principles.rule: Each piece says one thing, usually by joining two everyday symbols into a metaphor (molecule on a column, apple on a book, sound wave in a speech bubble).

principles.title: Space is content
principles.rule: One focal point and generous empty ground around it, at least 40% of the area. Centre it, or push it to one side to make room for words.

principles.title: Flat and honest
principles.rule: Flat colour from one Wada combination, black ink and white paper. No gradients, shadows, glows or 3D. The only tone is printed halftone dots.

principles.title: Plain symbols
principles.rule: Hands, eyes, books, suns, globes, columns, speech bubbles: things anyone recognises in a second, drawn simply.

principles.title: Warm, not cute
principles.rule: Friendly and a little playful, never childish. Wit comes from the idea, not from decoration.

principles.title: Gentle motion
principles.rule: Things are drawn on, pop in, blink or radiate in short loops, and always settle on a still frame.

layers.do: One Wada combination per piece: its background as the ground, its accent on at most one object. Ink is Black, paper is White.
layers.dont: Mix combinations in one piece, add gradients, tint the ink.

layers.do: Humanist typefaces: open, warm, very readable. Sentence case, few sizes, few weights. Type is set cleanly; the hand lives in the illustration.
layers.dont: Handwriting or 'marker' fonts, decorative display faces, many weights.

layers.do: A simple grid, wide margins, one focal point, text aligned to one edge. Illustration and headline work as a pair.
layers.dont: Filling every corner, boxes and borders around everything, centred paragraphs.

layers.do: Ink line over cut-paper shapes on a flat ground. One motif per piece.
layers.dont: Stock icons, perfect geometric vectors, detailed scenes, outlines with fills traced exactly inside them.

layers.do: Draw-on lines, popping shapes, small character beats; loops of 2 to 4 seconds.
layers.dont: Long sequences, camera moves, fades of the whole artwork, bouncy effects on text.

layers.do: Natural light, real people and hands, uncluttered backgrounds; cut-out photos on a flat ground fit the style.
layers.dont: Glossy stock, heavy filters, busy scenes.

layers.do: Plain, warm, short. Speak to one person (see the messaging playbook).

colorRoles.ground: Background of the chosen combination (role bg).
colorRoles.accent: Accent of the chosen combination: at most one object (the apple).

line.$comment: Thick marker or brush-pen line, even weight, round ends, slightly unsteady.
line.terminals: Round ends; ink dots (about the line width) mark joints and ends.

cutPaper.$comment: Filled shapes are scissor-cut: straight facets instead of smooth curves, slightly irregular, sitting a little off the line.

motion.$comment: Approximate readings of the 60 fps reference recordings.

draw.use: Ink lines drawing themselves on, start to end.

pop.use: Paper and accent shapes appearing with a small overshoot.

morph.use: One object turning into another (a frame into a book).

radiate.use: Dots growing into rays and travelling outward, repeating.

blink.use: Character beats: eyes close and open, then hold.

talk.use: Gentle pulse in a sound wave.

rules: Every animation ends on a still frame that works on its own.
Lines draw on; paper shapes pop on. Never fade the whole artwork in.
Loops are seamless and under 4 seconds.
With reduced motion, show the final frame.

references.shows: Sound wave in a speech bubble: voice. Centred motif, cut-paper bubble.
Molecule on an Ionic column: science with classical roots. Two symbols, one idea.
Two hands holding a globe: global connection. Motif pushed right, space left for text.
Frame draws on, apple pops in, frame turns into a book.
Dots grow into rays and radiate outward on a loop.
An eye at the end of a halftone beam blinks.
